source: User photographs of Português a Valer 3 glossary, pages 192, 194, 196, 198 and 200
normalization_notes: Assistant visual transcription of the Portuguese and English glossary columns only. German, Spanish, French, Chinese and internal lesson-page reference columns were not transcribed.

Keep printed articles, expressions and source English in rows. Remove article annotations from vocabulary entries; split expressions and pronominal clitics into individual words, keeping independent component translations.
Keep bem-sucedido as a lexical hyphenated compound. Lowercase and NFC-normalize words. Do not reduce other inflected forms to lemmas.
Book level B1 is user-supplied metadata; individual CEFR levels are assistant estimates, and may differ from B1.
Topic and grammatical groups only; book title and page numbers remain metadata. No database writes performed.
Two printed destaque rows are preserved and merged into one vocabulary entry with both senses.
Unclear internal reference digits were intentionally not guessed. Source photos are backed up for later inspection.
Estória is retained as the printed literary spelling; it is not silently changed to história. Cacimbo and bué are retained with regional/colloquial context in notes.

enrichment_provenance.english: Printed English retained verbatim in extracted rows and source_senses. Individual-word English reused where suitable; component translations and corrections by assistant.
enrichment_provenance.levels: Assistant CEFR estimates; no per-word levels supplied by the glossary.
enrichment_provenance.groups: Assistant thematic/grammatical classification using existing topic names.

corrections.note: The active verb is to call/name; the printed passive gloss belongs to ser apelidado.
Printed introduction is not the usual meaning of aplicação.
A stock cube is normally cubo de caldo; caldo alone means broth/stock.
Printed passive gloss corresponds to a reflexive/passive construction.
More precise standalone meaning than printed contradiction.
Printed dynamic is adjectival; the article marks a noun.

corrections.corrected_english: displaced; away from home; out of place
corrections.note: The Portuguese entry is an adjective, not an infinitive phrase.
Printed equivalent does not match the Portuguese noun.

corrections.corrected_english: to find strange; to be surprised at
corrections.note: Active verb: to find something strange.

corrections.corrected_english: to be busy with; to be working on
corrections.note: Printed return from can be misleading: estar de volta de algo commonly means to be busy working on it. Retain printed gloss for context.
Portuguese noun is normally feminine: a estalagmite. Preserve printed masculine article in extracted data.

uncertainties: The full context of estar de volta de is unavailable; both the printed return from gloss and the idiomatic busy with sense are retained. Only individually translated components are prepared.
Cacimbo is regional vocabulary, especially Angola; the source dry season sense is retained alongside fog.
Estória is a literary/regional variant; no spelling correction applied.
